questions.q: A feature in an AI vision model follows a normal distribution \( X \sim \mathcal{N}(25, 36) \). What is the mean \( \mu \) and variance \( \sigma^2 \) of this feature?
questions.answer: The notation \( \mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2) \) directly specifies the mean \( \mu = 25 \) and variance \( \sigma^2 = 36 \) (with standard deviation \( \sigma = 6 \)).

questions.q: Given \( n = 4 \) independent observations from a normal distribution with sum \( \sum_{i=1}^{4} x_i = 12 \), what is the Maximum Likelihood Estimate (MLE) \( \hat{\mu}_{\text{MLE}} \)?
questions.answer: The log-likelihood \( \ln L(\mu) = -\frac{n}{2}\ln(2\pi\sigma^2) - \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum (x_i - \mu)^2 \). Setting \( \frac{\partial \ln L}{\partial \mu} = 0 \) yields the sample mean \( \hat{\mu} = \frac{1}{n}\sum x_i = \frac{12}{4} = 3 \).

questions.q: In training a language model token predictor, a binary token occurs \( k = 3 \) times across \( n = 10 \) independent trials. What is the Maximum Likelihood Estimate \( \hat{p}_{\text{MLE}} \) of the token probability?
questions.answer: For a Bernoulli likelihood \( L(p) = p^k (1-p)^{n-k} \), the log-likelihood is \( \ln L = k\ln p + (n-k)\ln(1-p) \). Setting derivative to zero: \( \frac{k}{p} - \frac{n-k}{1-p} = 0 \implies \hat{p} = \frac{k}{n} = \frac{3}{10} = 0.300 \).
